newsitem.title: FRANCE: French parliament rejects wealth tax cap.
newsitem.headline: French parliament rejects wealth tax cap.

text.p: The French parliament on Tuesday killed a plan to limit a wealth tax on the very rich despite earlier backing for the idea from President Jacques Chirac and the centre-right majority.
A committee of members of the Senate and National Assembly, set up to reconcile differences between their two versions of the tax bill, voted by eight to five to drop the wealth tax cap.

The action ended a drawn-out quarrel over the measure, which was backed by the ruling coalition as needed to prevent capital flight but denounced by opposition Socialist and Communist deputies as a government gift to the ultra-rich.
The measure would have benefited France's 400 biggest fortunes which the government said should be encouraged to stay in France rather than made to flee to avoid taxes.

Until this year, the sum payable in wealth tax was limited to a maximum of 80 percent of a taxpayer's annual income. Then the conservative government raised the wealth tax by 10 per cent and removed the upper ceiling.
Chirac and Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure argued the ceiling should be restored, saying it had driven top millionaires to live outside of France for tax purposes.
The Senate accepted that argument, and National Assembly caucuses of both Chirac's Gaullist party and the junior UDF coalition party agreed last week to adopt the Senate move.
But backbenchers successfully argued it would be a political liability in times of austerity.

Centrist deputy Pierre Mehaignerie, who favoured the cap but refrained from voting on Tuesday, said afterwards that it had a negative impact on employment and urged the government to submit a new proposal.
